B. Schistosoma mansoni: Causes schistosomiasis, which can lead to chronic liver disease and gastrointestinal symptoms, but the acute presentation described here is not typical.
C. Campylobacter jejuni: Can cause gastroenteritis with diarrhea, but the systemic symptoms and rash are more characteristic of typhoid fever.
E. Clostridium perfringens: Causes food poisoning with diarrhea and abdominal cramps, but the systemic symptoms and travel history do not match.
